paragraphs.text: Red-green ( or RG ), also called Gruul , is an allied color pair. Red ( ) and green ( ) share a philosophy of intuition; they are the mutual enemies of blue ( ), the color of logic and foresight. Red-green is a combat -centric color pair that lends itself to midrange decks ; they share the evergreen keywords trample , haste , and reach .

As mutual enemies of blue , red and green have no patience for cold, calculating rationality. Their alliance is therefore about intuition. Red is the color of impulse, seeking happiness by acting on its emotions. Green is the color of instinct, fulfilling its natural role by acting on its inborn inclinations.

When paired, red and green care about living in the moment; red-green wants to participate in the messy, chaotic beauty of life with all its ups and downs. It believes that the key to happiness is following one's own internal compass, acting on instinct and emotion, and not worrying about the future. Red-green is the fastest, boldest color pair, prone to immediate action, and the quickest on its feet in novel situations. It is unafraid to make mistakes and learns best from experience. Neither red nor green is prone to reflection or long-term planning, which can cause trouble for red-green when it fails to anticipate the consequences of its own actions.

Red and green's disagreements mirror the black-white conflict of the good of the group versus the good of the individual. Green respects the interconnected web of life and is more drawn to community, while red's primary concern is itself. Green has a tranquil, passive side that is fundamentally at odds with red. On the other hand, green views red's destructive tendencies as dangerously out-of-sync with nature.
Examples of Red-green heroes include Samut and Wrenn , while villains include Agatha and Xenagos .

Red and green don't have as much mechanical overlap as some color pairs, but they complement each other in a midrange strategy , united by high- power creatures and a desire to attack . Ramp spells and efficient green creatures, backed up with red burn and Panic effects, allow red-green to push through damage and overwhelm its opponent in the mid-game. The trend toward straightforward midrange decks is strong, and it can be difficult to design for red-green in a way that allows for interesting strategic decisions. Because of the color pair's focus on combat, red-green creatures are easier to design than red-green noncreature spells.
The following mechanics are shared by red and green.
These multicolored cards best exemplify the strengths of red and green:
Hull Breach — Seamlessly combines red's artifact destruction and green's enchantment hate
Horned Kavu — Combines the two colors' love for cheap, mid-sized creatures
Decimate — Clearly demonstrates the colors' ability to deal with permanents of many types in an efficient way
